name: Flow React Next Integration (Ring Frontend Layer)

mission.primary_objective: Integrate Flow blockchain interactions into Ring Platform Next.js 16 App Router using @onflow/react-sdk with TypeScript-first hooks, wallet Connect UX, and sponsored transaction handoff to server payer where required.
mission.context: Ring uses React 19 Server Components by default. Flow wallet interactions are client-only. FlowProvider wraps the app; hooks (useFlowCurrentUser, useFlowMutate, useFlowQuery) handle queries and mutations. Distinguish @onflow/react-sdk from @xyflow/react (diagram UI).
mission.target_outcome: Ring clone pages show Connect wallet, user address, FT/NFT balances, and submit sponsored txs without EVM wagmi — consistent with flow_sponsored_transactions backend.
mission.scope: Client components, FlowProvider config, react-sdk hooks, flow.json contract deps — not Cadence contract source (flow_cadence_*) or server ensureWallet (flow_ensure_wallet_server).

truth_lens: Flow in Next.js is a client-island problem: FlowProvider and all mutate/query hooks live in 'use client' boundaries. Server Components may read off-chain Postgres wallet mapping from ensureWallet; on-chain reads use useFlowQuery with TanStack Query caching. Never import @onflow/fcl wallet auth in Server Actions without understanding server lacks browser wallet.
core_principles: Install @onflow/react-sdk; wrap app with FlowProvider + flow.json imports.
Use official Connect component for wallet discovery — do not build custom modal unless branding requires.
useFlowMutate for user-signed txs; combine with server-built payer authz for full sponsorship pattern.
WalletConnect: set walletconnectProjectId in FlowProvider when enabling WC option.
anti_patterns: Mounting FlowProvider in Server Component without client wrapper.
Calling useFlowMutate from Server Actions or RSC pages directly.
Hardcoding mainnet access node in test environments.
Expecting browser wallet to pay fees in production Ring (use sponsored payer).
key_patterns: flow-provider-wrapper.tsx: 'use client'; FlowProvider config={{ accessNodeUrl, flowNetwork, appDetailTitle, ... }} flowJson={flowJSON}.
useFlowQuery({ cadence, args }) for scripts; useFlowMutate for transactions.
useFlowTransaction(transactionId) for status tracking after mutate.
useFlowAuthz() returns wallet authorization fn for proposer/authorizer roles.
Starter reference: github.com/onflow/flow-react-sdk-starter (Next App Router + Testnet).
consult_when: Adding Flow wallet to Ring Platform Next.js clone
Configuring FlowProvider for mainnet vs testnet vs emulator
Choosing hooks for balance display vs NFT gallery vs transfer button
Integrating Connect with Ring Auth.js session (linked vs walletless)
expertise: FLOW_PROVIDER_SETUP — Next.js App Router client wrapper
REACT_SDK_HOOKS — query, mutate, current user, transaction status
RSC_BOUNDARY — server vs client split for Ring pages
role: LegioX truth lens — Flow React/Next.js integration
